A LITTLE ABOUT ME

About Me

I have always been drawn to the invisible threads that connect things — the patterns in nature, the stories of people, and the quiet details that reveal a larger world.

Hello, and welcome! I'm Amila Akagić (roughly pronounced AH-mee-lah AH-kah-gitch). I'm originally from Bosnia and Herzegovina, a small country in Southeastern Europe, but over the years, life and curiosity have taken me to many different corners of the world. I'm a university professor and researcher working in artificial intelligence, although my interests extend far beyond science.

I consider myself a citizen of the world. Living, studying, and working in different countries has given me the opportunity to meet wonderful people, experience different cultures, and discover new ways of looking at the world. Each of these experiences has shaped who I am, and this little corner of the internet is where I'd like to share some of them with you.

From an early age, I have been curious and observant, often fascinated by details that others might overlook. I have always been drawn to ideas, patterns, and the subtle connections that shape both nature and society. I can spend hours observing a particular phenomenon, studying its behavior, and trying to understand the principles behind it. What motivates me is not simply discovering how things work, but understanding why they work the way they do. I am particularly interested in the smallest threads that make up the fabric of our world, and how seemingly insignificant details can reveal something much larger about the systems, people, and societies around us.

A Life in Science

My professional life revolves around research, teaching, and exploring what technology can make possible. Much of my work has been in artificial intelligence, computer vision, and related fields.

What continues to interest me most is not simply developing new technologies, but understanding the questions behind them. Why do we approach problems in particular ways? What can we learn from other disciplines? And how can scientific progress contribute to a better understanding of the world?

I enjoy the intellectual freedom that research offers, especially when it leads me into unfamiliar territory.

Beyond the Laboratory

Outside academia, I have a rather eclectic mix of interests. I love traveling, especially to places with a rich and complicated history. I'm not much of a checklist traveler. I prefer wandering through unfamiliar streets, observing everyday life, and discovering the stories behind old buildings and traditions. If a place fascinates me, I might return several times, just to see how it changes with the light.

I'm equally drawn to literature, philosophy, music, art, nature, and sports. I have a habit of becoming deeply absorbed in whatever catches my attention, whether it's a historical event, a pattern in nature, or something curious about human behavior. I rarely stop at what; I usually want to know why.

I also collect quotations. I love those moments when a sentence written centuries ago expresses something I've been thinking but couldn't quite put into words. Perhaps that's what connects all my interests: a fascination with the details, the unexpected connections, and the stories beneath the surface.

Why I Write

For a long time, much of my writing has been academic: research papers, reports, lectures, and proposals. These forms of writing serve an important purpose, but they leave relatively little room for personal reflection.

I wanted to create a space where I could write differently.

Notes by Amila is a place to document experiences, preserve memories, explore ideas, and reflect on things that interest me, without necessarily having to arrive at a definitive conclusion.

Some notes will be about places I've visited. Others will concern science, books, art, or questions that emerge from ordinary life.

I don't expect everything here to fit neatly into one category. In fact, I rather like the idea that it won't.

A Few Words About This Space

This website is not intended to be a complete record of my life, nor a collection of carefully polished conclusions.

It is simply a place for things I find worth noticing, remembering, questioning, or sharing.

If something here makes you curious about a place, a book, an idea, or a different way of looking at the world, then perhaps these notes have served their purpose.
